prompt: Dá uma revisada nesse design doc que eu escrevi: docs/design/fanout-de-notificacoes.md. Pode aplicar direto as melhorias que não dependem de mim; o que precisar de informação minha, lista pra eu responder.
assertions: The review asks the author for a template reference before judging structure — since the user supplied none and templates normally live outside the repository, the question always goes to the author instead of treating the repo's silence as the answer
Structural additions are framed as suggestions from the skill's default catalog, not imposed as requirements, since no template governs the document
The reply separates findings into questions for the author versus edits applied
Missing trade-offs and alternatives become questions to the author — the edited doc gains no fabricated cons, alternatives, or metrics
A glossary is added or suggested at the BEGINNING of the document covering DLQ, TPS, CDC and SLA

The architecture diagram — whichever notation it ends up in, since the skill's convention replaces a hand-drawn Mermaid architecture with Structurizr DSL — is followed by explanatory prose, and no diagram is left orphaned
The out-of-scope items are no longer mere negations of goals: either rewritten honestly in the document, or explicitly raised to the author as a question in the reply
Vague goals ('melhorar a performance', 'garantir o SLA') are flagged as unmeasurable and the author is asked for numbers — no invented targets
The edited document remains in Portuguese and preserves the author's structure and voice
The header is honestly refreshed (Última atualização set to the real current date)

No invented technology: every technology, protocol, datastore and product named in the document — including inside a diagram's DSL technology slots and relationship labels — traces to the prompt or to the repository; unstated ones are left blank and raised as questions
